rationale: The deceptive kittens-birth report at PrS 83/55 is not good news; retain the inherited Russian observation and clarify that favorable news is usual, not required.

summary: Most examples announce welcome arrivals or recovered speech, but the already-quoted false kittens-birth report shows that the verb cannot require good news.
Recipients can be suffixal or bare nominal phrases; message content may follow in direct speech. l-marking can also identify the reporting actor in the Preterit.
The contracted kombašannolux at 69/579 is already in the entry and is a performative Infectum.
The occupational mbašər at 97/129 is kept outside the verbal entry pending confirmation; no collocation is independently established.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English accompanying the added examples is the supplied project machine translation, copied and cut without retranslation; lexical decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Round-1 broadening of good-news wording already accommodates announcement without requiring welcome content. It is not proposed again.
The recipient may be a bare name, reciprocal ḥḏoḏe or a personal suffix. Fronted bəšra can identify the announced theme independently of a recipient suffix.

mbašrone designates missionaries in nominal lists. Together with an absolute finite Mbašriwo it suggests specialised religious use, but nominal identity and machine 'preach' do not prove a new verbal paradigm or a Gospel-specific sense.
Confirm mbašər at 97/129 as the occupational noun related to Arabic mubāšir, rather than a verbal Imperativ.
The kittens-birth passage is supplied as PrS 83/55 and inherited as prs 242/6. Check whether the latter is page/line notation before changing its reference.
Confirm the actor/recipient segmentation in li emo mbašalla u babo at 111/44.
Jan 1.22/1136: who are the unexpressed subjects of Mbašriwo, and what do they announce? Confirm preaching from surrounding Turoyo before establishing a specialised verbal subsense.
Jan 2.28/4590,4593: confirm mbašrone as a missionary agent noun and its relation to the finite announcing verb; no Part act. box is added.
German typo: befal → befahl
rationale: The first-person singular past tense of befehlen is befahl; befal omits h.
